body:
Hi @NotWearingPants thanks for raising this issue. We'll look into our builds to check why MacOS and some specific architectures are using the release candidate versions of Cython. 

My guess is that we specify Cython bounds in our builds as `Cython<4.0.0rc1`, which were working fine previously, however a [recent change in pip](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/main/NEWS.rst#bug-fixes-3:~:text=The%20inclusion%20of,%2313163)) allows installing release candidate versions if the requirement specifies a release candidate in the requirement bounds.

I believe this is the cause for the release candidate versions of Cython being installed. Also coming to the memory leak issue with Cython, I believe it has now been fixed in Cython's patch version 3.1.1. Given that this is now the most recent version that satisfies our requirement constraints `Cython<4.0.0rc1`, I believe our artifacts from upcoming releases should automatically pick up the new Cython version and the memory leak should be solved too.
Thanks for the report, @NotWearingPants. We will update our build systems to pin cython to a stable version and re-release grpcio 1.71 and 1.72 as soon as we can.

> After a long investigation, it turns out this is neither my bug nor your bug nor macOS's fault, it's a https://github.com/cython/cython/issues/6878, because grpcio==1.71.0 was built with Cython==3.1.0a1 which is an unstable unreleased alpha version of Cython. 

Just to clarify, this bug doesn't just affect Cython==3.1.0a1. Unfortunately, stable Cython 3.1.0 is affected as well. We'll be pinning our Cython to 3.1.1.

issue.title: [Python] Pin Cython to 3.1.1

labels.name: release notes: yes
labels.description: Indicates if PR needs to be in release notes

repository.name: grpc
repository.description: C++ based gRPC (C++, Python, Ruby, Objective-C, PHP, C#)

issue.body:
This solves several issues:
1. #39588: Selecting unstable Cython releases when building gRPC Python artifacts.
2. Using inconsistent Cython version in released platform-specific wheels within the same grpcio release.
3. cython/cython#6878 Several published grpcio wheels were built with Cython 3.1.0 and are affected by Cython memory leak issue when using AsyncIO APIs (`grpc.aio.*`).

This change will be backported to 1.73.x, 1.72.x and 1.71.x.

Note: bazel Cython version wasn't upgraded because the latest cython BCR module version is still `3.0.11-1`.

body:
Thank you! Switching to `==` solves both problems. btw does this also explain why different platforms had different versions? Because even when using `<` if all builds run at the same time they should resolve to the same version, unless the Cython package has different latest versions for different platforms. Weird.

> this bug doesn't just affect Cython==3.1.0a1. Unfortunately, stable Cython 3.1.0 is affected as well.

Yeah, I discovered the bug before they released 3.1.0 (on `grpcio==1.71.0` with macOS, so `Cython==3.1.0a1`) but unfortunately it took me a while to report it and it made it to stable. Though it's pretty cool that `psycopg` has automated leak tests that caught the bug when 3.1.0 was published.

body: Thanks! This also bit me, memory crashing pretty quickly. Looking forward to a fix.
